2. QUANTITATIVE TIME BOUND AND CONTINUOUS CLOCK AT CRITICAL TOUCH

Keep epsilon=1, Q=lambda_*, k=lambda_*/R^2, and

  k0=k^(1/3)/(2^(7/3)B^(2/3)),
  F'<=-h[v]/2-A/2-D_y/2, D_y>=k0 L^(5/3).

All symbols and maximum bound Mbar have the definitions in v2. Integrating on
any lifetime interval yields

  integral h[v]<=2F0, integral A<=2F0,
  integral L^(5/3)<=2F0/k0.

Holder's inequality consequently gives, for every normalized time tau,

  integral_0^tau L <= (2F0/k0)^(3/5) tau^(2/5),
  integral_0^tau (lambda_*-lambda)
       <=6F0+d_clock tau^(2/5),
  d_clock=Mbar (2F0/k0)^(3/5).

The second inequality uses I=integral B qy<=Mbar L. It is stronger information
than the finite integral of lambda_- alone. Therefore

  rho(tau)>=rho0 exp[lambda_*tau-6F0-d_clock tau^(2/5)].

The elementary maximum over tau>=0 gives

  d_clock tau^(2/5)-(lambda_*/2)tau <= C_clock,
  C_clock=(3/5)d_clock[4d_clock/(5lambda_*)]^(2/3).

In particular the critical-touch branch obeys the explicit physical bounds

  1/(rho0 lambda_*) <= T-t0
        <=2 exp(6F0+C_clock)/(rho0 lambda_*),
  T-t(tau)<=2 exp(6F0+C_clock)/(rho0 lambda_*)
                                      exp[-lambda_*tau/2].

The lower bound holds because lambda<=lambda_*. The upper bound is derived
from the full memory dissipation; it is not inferred from integral lambda_-
alone. This improves the qualitative critical-time conclusion in v2/v3 and
does not change their proof of (T-t)rho->1/lambda_*.

Within the admitted positive physical C^(1+alpha) data set, T is continuous.
On each fixed normalized time interval, Amann's dependence theorem and the
exact scalar clock equations give continuous dependence of q,y,lambda,rho,t.
In a neighborhood of any admitted datum, rho0 has a positive lower bound,
F0 and M0,y0_max have common finite upper bounds, and the small entropy
condition stays strict. Hence the displayed exponential physical-time tail
bound is uniform in that neighborhood. Passing to the infinite clock interval
gives continuity of T. For epsilon<1 the original stricter exponential tail
from v2 (4.4) gives the same conclusion. No differentiability of T or uniform
exponential convergence of the gapless profile is claimed.

4. WHY THE CRITICAL MEMORY POWER IS A MECHANISM, NOT A LINEAR GAP

The critical estimate uses the measure of the region where the stationary
memory gap is small. More generally, if its gap delta(x)>=0 satisfies

  measure{x:delta(x)<s}<=C_gap s^r, 0<r<infinity,

the same split gives

  L<=sqrt(B_max C_gap s^r Y2)+P_y/s.

Optimizing s gives D_y=P_y+Y2>=c_gap L^p with

  p=(r+2)/(r+1)<2.

Therefore the positive quadratic error QL^2 is absorbed by D_y for small
initial entropy despite the absence of a uniform pointwise memory gap. A
one-dimensional quadratic contact has r=1/2 and p=5/3, exactly the proved
example. This deduction is an abstract entropy mechanism; a distinct full
material/profile construction for arbitrary contact geometry is not supplied.
It explains which quantitative geometric feature replaces the false spectral
gap assumption and why a positive-measure critical plateau is a different
case. The full theorem here is the explicit quadratic-contact family above.

CLAIM STATUS
The v2 continuum clock/entropy/critical mechanism, exact explicit static
construction and full-domain coercivity have been internally reconstructed
and checked by root/N25/natural director. The v3 weighted-Hilbert MR local
route was independently internally reviewed by N08. Section1 completes its
initial-time memory regularity interface; Sections2--4 are derived here.
This record does not turn those checks into external theorem validation or
empirical earthquake confirmation. The nonperiodic locked outer boundary,
arbitrary heterogeneity, supercritical W>1 branches and exact finite-time
moving zero fronts remain outside the established candidate theorem.
